briefs.task: Owner, 17 Nov 2026: 'Just do ray tracing and mesh shaders on mac, let's leave PC for now.' Plan hardware ray tracing (Metal ray queries / intersection) and mesh shaders (Metal object and mesh stages) on the Apple tile recipe, verified on this M3 Max, under the hardware-native decision (docs/design/decisions/HARDWARE-NATIVE-ENGINE.md): registry-selected accelerated paths, the portable path stays as fallback and reference, and each path is promoted only by a measured win. Decide from first principles and current state of the art which rendering problems in Thrum they should serve (for example GPU-driven geometry and culling, shadows, reflections, occlusion or GI) and whether this is a new module or milestones added to an existing one, following the module-decomposition rules. It must not delay V1 (SHOWCASE M8): schedule it off the critical path unless a piece clearly earns a place on it, and say which. Desktop high / PC stays out of scope; keep designs reusable for a later Vulkan/D3D12 recipe where that costs nothing. Done when the module list, a design and milestones with done-when files exist and are ready for design review.

The design review of MESH-SHADING at docs/evidence/MESH-SHADING/design-review.md asked for changes. Resolve its 5 Must Fix findings in the design and the plan. Its Suggestions are yours to take or leave; say which you took and why.

Also apply the owner's 17 Nov bar (see ORCHESTRATE.md if the bar change has landed): visual work passes on shipped-game look and speed with performance tripwires; references diagnose, never gate; proof proportional to risk.

The design review of MESH-SHADING at docs/evidence/MESH-SHADING/design-review.md asked for changes. Resolve its 4 Must Fix findings in the design and the plan. Its Suggestions are yours to take or leave; say which you took and why.

Lead: findings 2 and 3 return partly from the last round, both about the promotion machinery. Under the owner's 17 Nov bar (proof proportional to risk), prefer the simplest promotion rule that holds: an explicit, recorded per-device opt-in with a measured paired timing as a tripwire is acceptable; don't build general registry keying or exhaustive operand capture this module doesn't need. Off the V1 path.

The design review of MESH-SHADING at docs/evidence/MESH-SHADING/design-review.md asked for changes. Resolve its 2 Must Fix findings in the design and the plan. Its Suggestions are yours to take or leave; say which you took and why. This is round 3 and the module is converging, so take the smallest fix that removes each defect: an explicit portable recipe must stay on the portable path; for the frame timing, either measure the whole command-buffer GPU span or label the number as the pass interval it is. Timing is a tripwire under the owner's 17 Nov bar, not a gate.
